prompt_text:
Notes from PM Meeting: For each stage of the validation pipeline, what are the roles required to accomplish that stage from start to finish

From exploratory, design/scoping, implementation, prototyping, pilot data study, CDUT, protocol dev and running clinical study, and data review with fda, marketing and framing, polish and design.

CPM, IPM, PI, DS, SE, RA
Etc
You can put TBD if you don’t know.


6 sigma swim lanes flowcharts. 

Who gives final approval for go-no go for a project? Informed and consulted

Who decides which RND SD tickets get time
Are we going to chase this? Yes no

If yes:
Who comes up with the more informed question:hypothesis and who does it go to?
Who summarizes that information and who it’s presented to

How many SME interviews/reports are necessary so you decide you are done w exploration? How often do these get explored? Annually?

Where is the team focused?
What are their individual goals
How are we measuring success
What does good look like?


Discovery phase:
Documentation: Write up the history of the problem, when it occurs, which users are affected, what previous work has been done toward solving the problem, etc.

Design phase:

ask me questions to help me build a plan
response_text:
Below is a **first‑draft “validation‑pipeline playbook”** that pulls together everything you asked for (roles, decision‑rights, ticket‑gating, SME‑interview cadence, success metrics, etc.). I’ve kept the format modular so you can drop in or swap out items as you learn more about your organization’s exact titles and processes. --- ## 1. Validation‑Pipeline Stages & Required Roles | **Stage** | **Typical Deliverables** | **Core Roles (who does the work)** | **Support / Advisory Roles** | **Decision‑Gate Owner** | |-----------|--------------------------|-----------------------------------|------------------------------|--------------------------| | **Exploratory / Discovery** | Problem statement, user‑impact matrix, historical data dump, initial hypothesis list | **PM (CPM)** – drive interview schedule, capture notes
**Domain SME / Clinical Lead (PI)** – provide clinical context
**Data Scientist (DS)** – pull existing data, run quick descriptive stats
**Regulatory Analyst (RA)** – flag any known compliance constraints | **IPM (Innovation PM)** – ensure alignment with portfolio strategy
**UX/Design (SE)** – early user‑journey sketches (optional) | **IPM** (final “Go/No‑Go” for moving to design) | | **Design / Scoping** | Detailed use‑case flows, success criteria, risk register, high‑level architecture, resource estimate | **CPM** – create project charter & scope baseline
**PI** – define clinical endpoints & inclusion/exclusion criteria
**DS** – design data‑model & analytic plan
**SE** – system architecture, integration points
**RA** – draft regulatory pathway (e.g., 510(k), De Novo) | **Legal / IP Counsel** – early IP considerations
**Finance (PMO)** – budget sign‑off | **IPM + Finance Lead** (budget & strategic fit) | | **Implementation** | Build code, configure hardware, develop data pipelines, version‑controlled artifacts | **SE** – software/hardware development, CI/CD pipelines
**DS** – algorithm development, model training
**RA** – maintain regulatory traceability matrix
**CPM** – sprint planning & tracking | **QA / Test Engineer** – functional & performance testing
**Security Engineer** – threat modeling | **CPM** (with **IPM** as “final sign‑off” on scope adherence) | | **Prototyping** | Working prototype, usability test plan, early safety/efficacy signals | **SE** – integrate prototype into sandbox environment
**DS** – run pilot analytics, generate preliminary metrics
**PI** – conduct limited user testing (e.g., 5‑10 clinicians)
**RA** – confirm prototype stays within regulatory envelope | **Clinical Operations (CO)** – schedule user sessions
**UX Designer** – capture usability feedback | **PI** (clinical lead) + **CPM** (project health) | | **Pilot Data Study** | Formal pilot protocol, IRB/IEC approval, data collection plan, interim analysis report | **PI** – write pilot protocol, obtain IRB/IEC
**DS** – define statistical analysis plan (SAP)
**SE** – ensure data capture integrity, audit logs
**RA** – update regulatory submission package | **Biostatistician (optional)** – review SAP
**Safety Officer** – monitor adverse events | **IPM** (portfolio gate) + **Regulatory Lead** (RA) | | **CDUT (Clinical Data Usability Testing)** | Usability metrics, human‑factor analysis, final UI/UX tweaks | **PI** – lead clinical usability sessions
**SE** – implement UI changes
**DS** – analyze usability data (time‑on‑task, error rates) | **Human‑Factors Engineer** – formal usability report | **CPM** (go‑no‑go to full study) | | **Protocol Development & Full Clinical Study** | Full IND/IDE/IDE‑like protocol, CRO contracts, site‑selection, monitoring plan | **PI** – final protocol author, site‑lead liaison
**CPM** – CRO selection, schedule, budget tracking
**RA** – IND/IDE filing, FDA correspondence
**DS** – statistical analysis plan, DSMB data‑feeds | **Medical Writer** – protocol & informed‑consent docs
**Quality Assurance** – GCP compliance | **IPM** (strategic go‑no‑go) + **Regulatory Lead (RA)** (regulatory go‑no‑go) | | **Data Review with FDA** | FDA meeting minutes, submission of final data package, response to queries | **RA** – lead FDA interaction, compile submission
**PI** – answer clinical questions, provide raw data
**DS** – supply statistical outputs, validation reports
**CPM** – track timelines, action items | **Legal / IP Counsel** – review NDA/ licensing language | **RA** (final regulatory sign‑off) | | **Marketing & Framing** | Value proposition, market‑access dossier, launch plan, KOL briefings | **PM (CPM)** – coordinate cross‑functional launch team
**Marketing Lead** – messaging, positioning
**PI** – clinical evidence deck
**RA** – claim language compliance | **Health‑Economics Analyst** – cost‑effectiveness model
**Sales Ops** – territory planning | **CMO / VP of Commercial** (final go‑to‑market approval) | | **Polish & Design (Final Release)** | Final UI polish, documentation, training materials, post‑market surveillance plan | **SE** – final code freeze, performance hardening
**DS** – final model validation, bias audit
**RA** – post‑market surveillance SOPs
**CPM** – release checklist, training rollout | **Technical Writer** – user manuals
**Support Ops** – help‑desk prep | **CPM** (release sign‑off) + **IPM** (portfolio closure) | > **TBD** – If you have additional titles (e.g., “Clinical Operations Manager”, “Safety Officer”, “Biostatistician”) you can slot them into the “Support / Advisory” column. --- ## 2. 6‑Sigma Swim‑Lane Flowchart (High‑Level) Below is a **text‑based description** you can copy into any diagramming tool (Visio, Lucidchart, Miro, etc.). ``` +-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+ | CPM (PM) | PI (Clinical) | DS (Data Sci) | SE (Eng) | RA (Reg) | +-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+ | 1. Initiate | | | | | | - Capture | | | | | | stakeholder req| | | | | | - Draft charter | | | | | | - Gate Review | | | | | +-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+ | 2. Explore | 2a. Clinical SME | 2b. Data pull | 2c. System env | 2d. Regulatory | | - SME interviews| interviews | & quick stats | set‑up | impact scan | | - Problem doc | - Pain points | - Feasibility | - Tech stack | - Gap analysis | | - Hypothesis | - Clinical use | - Early model | - API mapping | - Pathway ID | +-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+ | 3. Design/Scope | 3a. Define endpoints|3b. Analytic plan|3c. Architecture |3d. Draft regulatory| | - Success crit | - Inclusion/Excl.| - Sample size | - Data flow | pathway doc | | - Risk register | - Clinical metrics| - KPI selection | - Security model | - Pre‑sub plan | | - Resource plan | | | | | +-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+ | 4. Prototype Test | 5a. Clinical pilot|5b. Pilot analytics|5c. Deploy prototype|5d. Regulatory | | - Usability | - Small user set | - Interim report | - Sandbox env | check‑in | | - Safety review | - Feedback loop | - Metric review | - Logging | - Sign‑off | +-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+ | 6. Pilot Study | 6a. Full protocol |6b. SAP & DSMB |6c. Data capture |6d. FDA pre‑sub | | - IRB/IEC | - Site contracts | - Power calc | - Audit trails | - Q‑sub | | - Enrollment | - Consent forms | - Interim analysis| - Monitoring | - Feedback | +-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+ | 7. FDA Review | 7a. Clinical Q&A |7b. Final stats |7c. Release notes |7d. Submission | | - Q‑sub pack | - Respond to | - Validation report| - Version tag | - FDA meeting | | | FDA queries | - Sensitivity | - Deploy to prod | - Decision memo | +-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+ | 8. Market Launch | 8a. Value prop |8b. Evidence deck |8c. Final UI/UX |8d. Claim language| | - KOL briefings | - Clinical ROI | - Publication | - Training kits | - Compliance check| | - Sales enable | - Publication plan| - Posters | - Support docs | - Sign‑off | +-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+ | 9. Post‑Launch | 9a. Post‑market |9b. Real‑world |9c. Bug triage |9d. Surveillance | | - Surveillance | - Safety reporting| - Data ops | - Patch releases | - Periodic audit | +-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+ ``` *Each **lane** (column) represents a functional role. The **rows** are the 6‑Sigma “Define‑Measure‑Analyze‑Improve‑Control” phases mapped to your validation pipeline. You can add “Decision Gate” boxes after rows 2, 4, 6, and 8 – those are the **Go/No‑Go** checkpoints.* --- ## 3. Decision‑Authority Matrix | **Decision** | **Who Gives Final Approval?** | **Informed (I)** | **Consulted (C)** | |--------------|------------------------------|------------------|-------------------| | **Go/No‑Go to Design** | **IPM (Innovation Portfolio Manager)** | CPM, PI, SE, DS, RA | Executive Sponsor, Finance | | **Ticket‑Prioritization (R&D/SD tickets)** | **R&D Steering Committee** (usually chaired by **CPM** with **IPM** as voting member) | All functional leads (PI, DS, SE, RA) | Product Marketing, Legal | | **Chase the ticket? (Yes/No)** | **CPM** (with sign‑off from **IPM** if budget impact) | R&D leads | Finance, Legal | | **Formulating the “Informed Question / Hypothesis”** | **PI** (clinical lead) drafts the clinical hypothesis; **DS** refines the data‑science question. | CPM, SE | RA (to ensure regulatory‑compatible wording) | | **Where does the hypothesis go?** | **Project Charter** → stored in the **PMO repository**; shared with **IPM** and **Regulatory Lead** for review. | | **Summarizing & Presenting Findings** | **CPM** prepares the executive summary; **PI** presents clinical relevance; **DS** presents analytics. | IPM, R&D Steering Committee | FDA (when at submission stage), Marketing, Legal | | **Number of SME Interviews / Reports to Close Exploration** | **Rule‑of‑Thumb:** *Minimum 5 distinct SME personas* (e.g., clinician, nurse, IT admin, patient advocate, payer).
**Stop‑criteria:** saturation (no new themes after 2 consecutive interviews) **AND** a **risk‑impact matrix** that scores ≤ 2 on “unknowns”. | CPM, PI | IPM (to sign‑off) | | **Exploration Review Cadence** | **Quarterly** (or after any major market/clinical change). | All functional leads | Executive Sponsor | | **Team Focus (Current Sprint)** | **CPM** sets the sprint goal; **PI** ensures clinical relevance; **DS** ensures data‑readiness; **SE** ensures technical feasibility; **RA** ensures compliance. | All | IPM | | **Individual Goals** | See Section 4 (KPIs). | — | — | | **Measuring Success** | See Section 4. | — | — | | **What “Good” Looks Like** | See Section 4. | — | — | --- ## 4. Success Metrics & “What Good Looks Like” | **Metric** | **Owner** | **Target / Acceptance Criteria** | **Measurement Cadence** | |------------|-----------|----------------------------------|--------------------------| | **Clinical Feasibility** | PI | ≥ 80 % of target clinicians rate prototype “clinically useful” (Likert ≥ 4/5) | End of Prototype phase | | **Regulatory Pathway Alignment** | RA | No “major deficiency” letters from FDA pre‑submission | Pre‑submission checkpoint | | **Model Performance** | DS | Sensitivity ≥ 90 % & Specificity ≥ 85 % on pilot data (with 95 % CI) | Pilot Data Study | | **Technical Reliability** | SE | < 1 % critical bugs in production (post‑launch 90‑day window) | Continuous monitoring | | **Budget Adherence** | CPM | ≤ 5 % variance vs. approved budget | Monthly financial review | | **Time‑to‑Market** | IPM | ≤ 18 months from Go‑Design to FDA clearance | Milestone tracking | | **Stakeholder Satisfaction** | CPM | ≥ 85 % satisfaction in post‑project survey (all functional leads) | End‑of‑project | | **Market Adoption** | Marketing | ≥ 30 % of target sites adopt within 6 months of launch | Quarterly sales/usage reports | | **Post‑Market Safety** | RA | ≤ 0.5 % serious adverse event rate (per 1,000 uses) | Ongoing surveillance | **What “Good” Looks Like (Narrative):** A “good” validation pipeline delivers a clinically‑validated, regulatorily‑cleared solution **on time, on budget, and with demonstrable user value**. The product should achieve pre‑defined performance thresholds on the pilot, receive a clean FDA clearance (or CE mark, depending on market), and see **early adopter uptake** (> 30 % of the addressable market) within the first six months. Internally, the cross‑functional team should report high satisfaction, minimal re‑work, and clear documentation that enables rapid post‑launch iteration. --- ## 5. Discovery‑Phase Documentation Checklist | **Section** | **What to Capture** | **Owner** | |-------------|---------------------|-----------| | **Problem History** | When the problem first surfaced, prior attempts (internal & external), regulatory notices, market reports | CPM | | **User Impact** | User personas, frequency of occurrence, pain‑point severity (e.g., “high‑risk” vs. “low‑risk”) | PI + UX/SE | | **Clinical Context** | Disease/condition description, standard of care, unmet need, clinical workflow mapping | PI | | **Existing Evidence** | Literature review, prior patents, competitor solutions, FDA guidance documents | RA + DS | | **Data Landscape** | Sources (EHR, claims, device logs), data quality, gaps, access constraints | DS | | **Regulatory Landscape** | Device classification, predicate devices, guidance documents, pre‑submission opportunities | RA | | **Business Rationale** | Market size, reimbursement pathways, ROI estimate, strategic fit | CPM + Marketing | | **Preliminary Hypotheses** | Clinical hypothesis, data
